user.text: When navigating from the dashboard to a project, I want the project's title to appear instantly, but I don't want to prefetch the rest of the project page.

history.assistant:
Done. The title now appears instantly on navigation while the rest of the project page is not prefetched.

## What was wrong before
The project page fetched the title and the slow details together in one `Promise.all`, wrapped in a single `Suspense`. With `cacheComponents` enabled, the PPR shell was just `"Loading project..."` — the title waited 800ms for the details.

## Changes

**`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`** — split into two independent Suspense boundaries:
- `<ProjectTitle>`: fast, static (`getProjectTitle` is `'use cache'`), so it gets baked into the prerendered shell.
- `<ProjectDetails>`: opts into request-time streaming via `await connection()` from `next/server`, so it becomes a dynamic streaming hole that is never prefetched.
- Added `generateStaticParams` (from the new `projectSlugs` export) so each project's slug-specific title shell is prerendered at build time and eligible for link prefetch.

**`lib/data.ts`** — exported `projectSlugs` for `generateStaticParams`.

**`app/page.tsx`** — unchanged. The dashboard `<Link>` keeps default prefetch, which under PPR prefetches only the static title shell — not the dynamic details.

## Verification
- `npm run build` passes (TypeScript clean). Route table now shows `◐` Partial Prerender for `/projects/acme` and `/projects/orbit`.
- The prerendered HTML shell for `/projects/acme` contains `Acme Storefront` (the title, instant) followed by `Loading details…` (the streaming placeholder). So on navigation the title shows immediately from the prefetched shell, and the description + activity stream in only after the user actually navigates (~800ms later).

Note: `next build` also auto-reconfigured `tsconfig.json`/`package.json` (its mandatory changes) and generated `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, `package-lock.json` — those are build artifacts, not part of the source change.
